content:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 2% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 0.3–0.8% bias to early forecast.
- Model overestimates in late horizon (25–30 days) when sentiment is positive; reduce final 5–7 days by 0.5–1.2%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.2–0.6% upward bias to next forecast.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce by 0.5–1.0%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
